mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved steadily from -14.7 to -9.0 over the prior three weeks, reflecting a gradual re-normalization of shopping and leisure activity. This underlying momentum continues independent of any single trigger, pushing the next-4-week mean of RETAIL_REC above the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -14.7 (t-3w) to -9.0 (t-1w) before a small pullback to -10.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the last-28-day mean despite the three-week improving trend, the always-on momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week collapse in TRANSIT mobility signals reduced commuter and errand-linked movement that feeds retail footfall. When TRANSIT drops more than 15 points in a single week (as observed from -15.4 to -20.6 at t-1w), the associated loss of incidental shopping trips depresses RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -15.4 (t-2w) to -20.6 (t-1w), a drop of 5.2 points, approaching but not exceeding the trigger in this snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the two weeks following a TRANSIT drop exceeding 15 points, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous sharp drop in WORKPLACES and spike in RESIDENTIAL (as seen at t-1w: WORKPLACES -22.7, RESIDENTIAL +12.9) indicates a holiday or episodic stay-home event. When both series revert toward baseline in the subsequent week (as observed at t-0w), pent-up demand is released into retail and recreation activity, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 15 points while RESIDENTIAL rises more than 3 points in the same week, followed by partial reversal
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES swung from -4.1 to -22.7 and back to -3.4, while RESIDENTIAL peaked at 12.9 in the same week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the two weeks after the WORKPLACES/RESIDENTIAL reversal, the pent-up-demand interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Deep and persistent negative readings in both PARKS and TRANSIT indicate active mobility restrictions or public caution consistent with a tightening policy regime. Under this regime, retail recovery stalls or reverses because non-essential movement remains suppressed, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained below -15 in three of four weeks and TRANSIT never exceeded -14.9
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite PARKS and TRANSIT remaining persistently depressed, the policy-suppression mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The one-week anomaly at t-1w (WORKPLACES -22.7, RESIDENTIAL +12.9, PARKS improving to -8.3) is consistent with a recurring calendar holiday. Seasonal mean-reversion predicts that the week immediately following the snapshot will show a rebound in retail-linked movement as normal weekday routines resume, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL both show a single-week outlier at t-1w consistent with a holiday calendar effect
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase in the first week following the holiday-pattern anomaly, the seasonal reversion mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains comparatively less negative or positive relative to RETAIL_REC, consumers are substituting essential grocery trips for discretionary retail and recreation outings. This substitution pattern, visible in weeks where GROCERY_PHARM turned positive (0.4 and 3.1) while RETAIL_REC stayed deeply negative, suppresses RETAIL_REC recovery over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 0 while RETAIL_REC remains below -8
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 0.4 and 3.1 in t-2w and t-1w while RETAIL_REC stayed between -9.0 and -11.7
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises during weeks when GROCERY_PHARM is positive, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility acts as a substitute for indoor retail and recreation activity; when PARKS rises sharply (as it did from -18.9 to -8.3), outdoor-seeking behavior temporarily displaces indoor retail visits, and when PARKS subsequently falls back (as it did to -15.6), displaced demand returns to retail, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -18.9 to -8.3 then fell back to -15.6 within two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week after PARKS reverts downward from a local peak, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Synchronized recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals a broader reopening of commuting and economic activity that compounds to drive stronger retail and recreation recovery than either series alone would predict. When both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve in the same week, as at t-0w (WORKPLACES from -22.7 to -3.4, TRANSIT from -20.6 to -14.9), the combined effect raises RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve by more than 5 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved by 19.3 points and TRANSIT improved by 5.7 points in the same week (t-0w)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite simultaneous WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improvement, the compounded-reopening interaction mechanism is rejected.
